([[Sussex, Wisconsin]]) | college = [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Patrick O'Neal Baldwin Jr.''' (born November 18, 2002), nicknamed "'''PBJ'''", is an American [[college basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee Panthers]] of the [[Horizon League]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. ==High school career== Baldwin played basketball for [[Sussex Hamilton High School|Hamilton High School]] in [[Sussex, Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last1=Radcliffe |first1=JR |title=Top-flight freshman Patrick Baldwin Jr. is just part of the youth movement as Hamilton basketball starts season 2–0 |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/communities/northwest/sports/2017/11/26/top-flight-freshman-patrick-baldwin-jr-just-part-youth-movement-hamilton-basketball-starts-season-2/896629001/ |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=November 26, 2017}} During his freshman year he was part of their 2017–18 team that made the state championship, losing to [[Oshkosh North High School|Oshkosh North]].{{Cite web|title=HHS Boys’ Basketball 2017–18 Season|url=https://hamiltonchargers.sportngin.com/page/show/4170560-2017-18-season|url-status=live}} As a junior, Baldwin averaged 24.3 points and 10.8 rebounds per game, earning Wisconsin [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web |last1=Masson |first1=Jon |title=Sussex Hamilton's Patrick Baldwin Jr. earns Gatorade state player of the year honor for boys basketball |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/sussex-hamiltons-patrick-baldwin-jr-earns-gatorade-state-player-of-the-year-honor-for-boys/article_ae4f0b83-ab0a-59c5-ac07-1d465c9308e0.html |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=March 27, 2020}} During the second game of his senior season, Baldwin suffered a season-ending ankle injury.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Sidelined with Season-Ending Injury, SI99 Wing Patrick Baldwin Jr. Focused on Recruitment |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/patrick-baldwin-decision-looms-si99-duke-northwestern-uw-milwaukee-kentucky |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=December 14, 2020}} He was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last1=Hogg |first1=Curt |title=Two players from Wisconsin are named to the boys McDonald's All American Game |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2021/02/23/patrick-baldwin-jr-michael-foster-jr-named-mcdonalds-all-americans/4562887001/ |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Baldwin was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. On May 12, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] under the coaching of his father over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. He was also the youngest person ever to receive an offer to play at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], receiving the offer in his sophomore year of high school. {{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Elite Prep Wing Patrick Baldwin Jr. Commits to UW-Milwaukee |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/patrick-baldwin-commits-uw-milwaukee |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 12, 2021 |date=May 12, 2021}} He became the highest-rated recruit to ever commit to a [[Horizon League]] program.{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Givony |first2=Jonathan |title=Five-star college basketball recruit Patrick Baldwin to play for father at Milwaukee |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31432017/five-star-recruit-patrick-baldwin-play-father-milwaukee |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 12, 2021 |date=May 12, 2021}} {{College career== In his college debut, Baldwin posted 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 75–60 win against [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|North Dakota]].{{cite news |title=Baldwin's double-double leads Milwaukee past North Dakota |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365588 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 10, 2021}} On November 23, 2021, he suffered a leg injury in a loss to [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]], forcing him to miss several games.{{cite news |last1=Rosiak |first1=Todd |title=Bowling Green 82, UWM 68: Patrick Baldwin Jr. misses most of the second half with leg injury |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uwm/2021/11/23/bowling-green-82-uw-milwaukee-68-patrick-baldwin-jr-injured/8731006002/ |access-date=November 29, 2021 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=November 23, 2021}} Baldwin suffered an ankle injury on January 5, 2022, in a 63–49 win against [[Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball|Green Bay]].{{cite news |last1=Rosiak |first1=Todd |title=UWM 63, UWGB 49: Panthers smother Phoenix for second straight win, but Patrick Baldwin Jr. is hurt again |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uwm/2022/01/05/uw-milwaukee-63-uw-green-bay-49-panthers-defense-key-victory/9101640002/ |access-date=January 25, 2022 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=January 5, 2022}} Baldwin returned on February 4, 2022 in a 70-60 loss to IPFW, where he shot 5-15, and 1-6 from 3. He also played the next two conference games against Cleveland State and Northern Kentucky, averaging 30 minutes and 6.5pts while shooting 4-19 overall (1-11 from 3), before sitting out the rest of the season for undisclosed reasons. On April 22, 2022, Baldwin declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Patrick Baldwin Jr. entering NBA draft after injury-marred season at Milwaukee|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33784271/patrick-baldwin-jr-entering-nba-draft-injury-marred-season-milwaukee|date=April 22, 2022|accessdate=April 22, 2022}} ==National team career== Baldwin represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 7.7 points and five rebounds per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Patrick Baldwin Jr (USA)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Patrick-Baldwin-Jr |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 12, 2021}} ==Personal life== Baldwin's father, [[Pat Baldwin (basketball)|Pat]], was a standout college basketball player at [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] and is the former head coach at [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]].{{cite web |last1=Greenstein |first1=Teddy |title=Top recruit Patrick Baldwin has 'home visit' with his father |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-patrick-baldwin-recruit-zoom-home-visit-20200506-v7diicx4ljbufhiu4y7jki5pmq-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=May 6, 2020}} His mother, Shawn, played [[volleyball]] at Northwestern.{{cite web |last1=Greenstein |first1=Teddy |title=Where will No. 3 basketball recruit Patrick Baldwin Jr. sign? |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-patrick-baldwin-northwestern-duke-milwaukee-20200219-tgjq5obywzdatnkdjig4zwv7hy-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=April 11, 2021 |date=February 19, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://mkepanthers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/patrick-baldwin-jr-/11548 Milwaukee Panthers bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/baldwin-jr-patrick.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Baldwin, Patrick Jr.}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Wisconsin]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Waukesha County, Wisconsin]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from the Milwaukee metropolitan area]]
